meaning:
ἐλευθερία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Lev.19:20 (חֻפְשָׁה), 1Es.4:49 Est.4:53, Sir.7:21, Sir.33:25, 1Ma.14:27, 3Ma.3:28 * ;]
liberty: with reference to the religious life, 1Co.10:29, 2Co.3:17, Gal.2:4 5:1, 1Pe.2:16, 2Pe.2:19; ὁ νόμος τῆς ἐ., Jas.1:25 2:12; ἡ ἐ. τῆς δόξης, Rom.8:21; ἐπ᾽ ἐ., Gal.5:13 (on which formula, cf. Deiss., LAE, 327 ff.; Cremer, 251).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: that the creation itself also will be delivered from the bondage of decay into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.
Conscience, I say, not your own, but the other’s conscience. For why is my liberty judged by another conscience?
Now the Lord is the Spirit and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
This was because of the false brothers secretly brought in, who stole in to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into…
But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets, but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he…
as free, and not using your freedom for a cloak of wickedness, but as bondservants of God.
promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him.
